description: Surrogate primary key. Sequential, generated at table creation.
Self-referencing foreign key to meteorite_classification.id; empty only for the root (Meteorites).
Hierarchy level from Fig. 1 rows. One of: root, division, class, clan, group, subgroup.
Short label/abbreviation as printed in the Fig. 1 box (e.g. an iron group or clan code).
Expanded or descriptive name for the node.
Number of edges from the root; root = 0. Derived from parent_id chain.
Slash-delimited chain of ids from root to node, with leading and trailing '/'. Supports prefix descendant queries, e.g. WHERE materialized_path LIKE '/1/4/%'.
Human-readable slash-delimited chain of codes from root to node.
Short prose description of the node, paraphrased from the cited source(s). For classes/clans, describes the grouping concept; for groups/subgroups, the defining petrologic/chemical traits.
example: Karoonda-type; matrix-rich, highly oxidized C chondrites...

description: Primary literature source(s) for the description.
Transcription/provenance notes (e.g. nodes connected directly to a division, or grouping connectors unlabeled in the figure).
Foreign key to meteorite_classification.id; an ancestor (or the node itself).
Foreign key to meteorite_classification.id; a descendant (or the node itself).
Number of edges from ancestor to descendant. 0 = self-reference (every node has one).
The single root node (Meteorites, id 1) has an empty parent_id and a self-pair at depth 0 in the closure table.
PAL (Pallasites) and IRON (Irons) are clan-level nodes added to capture shared connectors that are unlabeled in Fig. 1; flagged in notes.
Some group nodes (R, K, URE, BRA, ANG, AUB, MES) attach straight to a division box in Fig. 1 with no intervening class/clan; their parent_id points to the division.
Weisberg M. K., McCoy T. J., Krot A. N. (2006) Systematics and Evaluation of Meteorite Classification, Fig. 1, p. 21.
